profile.campus: Eagle Mountain, Utah County, Utah (Meta's Eagle Mountain data center campus, five original buildings expanding to a reported total of roughly 4.5 million square feet across a multi-phase build-out)
profile.address: Pony Express Parkway, Meta Eagle Mountain Data Center, Eagle Mountain, Utah County, Utah, 84005
profile.reading: This Meta data center building (building 4 of 5 mapped in this cluster, westernmost to easternmost ordering) is part of Meta's Eagle Mountain campus in Utah County, southwest of Salt Lake City. Meta announced the project in May 2018 and brought the first phase online on July 14, 2021, per Meta's own announcement; that initial build totaled nearly 2.4 million square feet across five buildings, generated more than 1,250 peak construction jobs, and now supports more than 200 permanent jobs, with over $1 billion invested in Utah upon completion of that phase. A Phase 3 expansion announced in September 2022 raised total planned investment to $1.5 billion and added roughly 2 million more square feet across two additional structures, pushing the eventual completed campus toward about 4.5 million square feet, according to the Deseret News. Utah County and the Alpine School District approved property-tax incentive agreements potentially worth up to $750 million in relief across all five planned phases over roughly 40 years, including 100% relief on personal property taxes and 80% relief on real property taxes in Phase 1 alone; the school district capped its own contribution at $40 million per phase and $120 million total. On sustainability, Meta says the campus is designed to use 80% less water than an average data center, recycled more than 85% of construction waste, and partnered with Rocky Mountain Power to develop more than 800 megawatts of new solar generation capacity through nine projects spanning Iron, Tooele, and Carbon counties, work Meta says created more than 1,400 construction jobs and $260 million of local investment. Meta also partnered with Trout Unlimited in 2020 on a Provo River restoration project intended to keep 416 million gallons of water in the river during the hottest months. Meta reports about $2 million in community contributions since the 2018 groundbreaking, including nearly $1 million to schools, small businesses, and nonprofits. Meta does not publish a specific street address, exact per-building square footage, or facility codes for individual Eagle Mountain structures; the address above is derived from reverse-geocoding this building's mapped coordinates, not from an operator-published source, and should be treated as approximate.

sources.title: Facebook parent Meta announces mega expansion to Eagle Mountain data center project

profile.capacity_note: Meta does not publish per-building IT capacity or MW figures for Eagle Mountain; the campus overall was reported at nearly 2.4 million square feet across five buildings for Phase 1, growing toward roughly 4.5 million square feet with the Phase 3 expansion announced in 2022. No per-building figure is asserted here.
profile.facility_note: One of five Meta buildings OpenStreetMap groups together at this Eagle Mountain location.

profile.regional_context: Eagle Mountain, in the fast-growing western Utah County/Salt Lake City exurbs, has drawn additional data center development beyond Meta: Tract announced plans for a roughly 400-megawatt data center park in the same city, according to Data Center Dynamics and the Daily Herald, reflecting the area's access to power infrastructure and available land. Utah's incentive structure for large data centers, including the multi-decade Alpine School District and Utah County tax agreements covering Meta's phased build-out, has been a recurring subject of local reporting.

reading.body:
Meta operates a facility at Pony Express Parkway in Eagle Mountain, Utah County, but publishes no power capacity figure for this site. The research note indicates the facility exists and belongs to Meta's owned-and-operated data center program, though opening date, investment, and building specifications were not confirmed in available sources. This campus ranks tenth among Utah facilities with published megawatt figures, a designation that reflects the absence of a disclosed capacity rather than a measured ranking.

Utah holds 21 mapped data center facilities, of which only nine publish power specifications totaling 52.18 MW. The state's relatively low published capacity and the dominance of non-publishing sites suggest that most Utah data centers operate under confidential specifications. Without a published figure, this Meta facility cannot be assessed for its contribution to Utah's AI infrastructure or to the state's grid constraints.

Meta's broader data center program, described in available sources as multi-billion dollar in scale and recently characterized by a separate 10 billion dollar investment in Louisiana, indicates the company prioritizes data center expansion at the national level. Whether Eagle Mountain serves Meta's AI compute, inference, or other workloads remains unpublished. The facility's significance to AI scaling cannot be determined from disclosed specifications.
